A Hindu group visited the Eiffel Tower to pray. Women told to ‘step aside’

The instructions during a BAPS delegation’s private visit sparked a staff strike and a political backlash in France.

Himanshi Aggarwal

08 September, 2026 10:21 am IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

Swami Keshavvandas, the sixth and current spiritual guru of the BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha, at the Eiffel Tower on Saturday | Photo: @BritIndianVoice/X

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

New Delhi: The Eiffel Tower was closed to the public on Monday after staff staged a strike in protest over the treatment of female employees during a visit by a Hindu religious delegation. Women workers at the site were reportedly asked to leave their workstations or stay out of sight during the visit, according to workers and management.

According to reports, a group of around 100 people linked to the Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha (BAPS) was visiting as part of events linked to the inauguration of a new temple near Paris. Union representative Diane Davoine said women were instructed to step aside so male colleagues could take their places as the delegation passed through.

“During the visit of this delegation, women were asked to leave their places of work in order to place men there,” Davoine told Reuters. She also said management had apologised to workers over the incident.

Show Full Article

“So that absolutely does not go down well with the employees, with women obviously, who are all humiliated by what happened, by the way some were treated,” she said.

She added: “Tensions mounted over the weekend, so this morning, the employees decided to meet: first, to open a dialogue with management, and second, to ensure that women are never treated this way at the company again.”

In a statement, staff condemned “professional instructions that led to female employees being sidelined, replaced and made invisible because of their sex”. Some workers were reportedly told to withdraw to other areas or avoid certain zones while the group was present. The delegation was accompanied only by male staff on parts of the visit, including the third floor.

The Société d’Exploitation de la Tour Eiffel (SETE), which operates the monument, confirmed that the delegation had requested that the visit be organised to limit “interactions with women”. SETE said those conditions “should not have been accepted” and that management had apologised to staff. SETE president Ariel Weil said the company would investigate and “draw the necessary conclusions”.

Paris Mayor Emmanuel Grégoire called the arrangement “unacceptable”.

“It is not acceptable that such conditions can be tolerated,” he wrote in a post on X. “These are neither my values, nor those that the Eiffel Tower should uphold, where everyone—regardless of gender—should be able to move about and act freely, without distinction between women and men.”

“I refuse to allow women to be compelled to step aside in order to meet the demands of foreign visitors,” Yaël Braun-Pivet, the president of the National Assembly, wrote in a post on X. “In France, women fully occupy public spaces. No one dictates to them that they must become invisible there.”

The BAPS temple in Paris later issued a statement saying it took the concerns “very seriously”.

“To the best of our knowledge, at no point was anyone prevented access to the Eiffel Tower,” the statement read. “Nevertheless, we sincerely apologise for any pain or inconvenience caused.”

(Edited by Prashant Dixit)

Paris probes claim that women staff told to step out of sight as Hindu delegation visited Eiffel Tower

Union says female employees were asked to stay out of sight during Hindu group’s private visit; Paris authorities investigating the incident

Reuters

08 September, 2026 09:43 am IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

Representative Image

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

Paris: Female employees at the Eiffel Tower were asked to step out of sight during a visit by a Hindu religious delegation at the weekend, according to union representatives, prompting a staff protest and an investigation by Paris city authorities.

The monument was closed late on Monday as employees held a meeting over the incident, which has angered staff and drawn criticism from French politicians.

On Saturday, a delegation of about 100 people linked to the Hindu group Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha, or BAPS, made a private visit to the Eiffel Tower.

“As the delegation passed through, women were asked to leave their workstations so that men could take their places,” Diane Davoine, a union representative, told Reuters.

“Tensions mounted over the weekend, so this morning, the employees decided to meet: first, to open a dialogue with management, and second, to ensure that women are never treated this way at the company again,” she said.

Show Full Article

Signs at the base of the tower on Monday read: “The opening of the Eiffel Tower is delayed for operational reasons.” Davoine said management apologised to staff over the incident.

Paris Mayor Emmanuel Gregoire said that an investigation would be launched “as soon as possible”. In a post on social media platform X, he said he was aware of the employees’ anger and agreed their dissatisfaction was legitimate.

“It is urgent that all light be shed on the facts that led to this protest,” Gregoire wrote.

BAPS, whose representatives were in France for festivities related to the inauguration of a Hindu temple in the Paris suburbs, said in a statement that the visit to the Eiffel Tower was arranged at the start of opening hours to avoid disrupting others, due to the size of its delegation.

“To the best of our knowledge, at no point was anyone prevented access to the Eiffel Tower. Nevertheless, we sincerely apologise for any pain or inconvenience caused,” the statement said.

A spokesperson for SETE, the company operating the monument, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Yael Braun-Pivet, the president of the National Assembly, wrote in a post on X: “Welcoming others never means giving up our values. In France, women are fully present in public life. No one tells them to become invisible.”

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

By Stefica Nicol Bikes CLARENCE TOWN, Australia, Sept 8 (Reuters) – Australian firefighters say they are on alert as temperatures in the southern hemisphere begin to pick up, following a devastating fire season in Europe.

Australia is already experiencing a strong El Nino weather event that typically brings with it hotter, drier weather, and an increased risk of wildfires.

“We’re concerned this year that we’ll see increased fire risk (versus) prior years,” said Trent Curtin, head of the New South Wales Rural Fire Service, the world’s largest volunteer firefighting force.

Show Full Article

Large parts of Europe, the world’s fastest-warming continent, endured sweltering summers, leaving vegetation tinder-dry and fuelling severe wildfires.

Britain had its hottest summer since records began, with Italy’s the warmest for 75 years.

“We’re seeing some extraordinary conditions in the northern hemisphere at the moment,” Curtin said.

“They’re experiencing fires that they haven’t seen for a couple of decades or maybe never seen before.”

Australia has a long history of fighting wildfires, including the 2019 to 2020 Black Summer blazes that destroyed an area the size of Turkey and killed 33 people.

Authorities frequently conduct hazard reduction burns, where sections of forest are burnt in a controlled manner to reduce the spread of wildfires should they happen.

“For this year we’re alert but not alarmed. We’re conscious of the fact that the seasonal outlook is expecting a busier than usual fire season – conditions will be quite dry, hot,” said Alex Capararo, a sector commander for the Forestry Corporation of New South Wales, which manages state-owned land, as he led a hazard reduction burn around three hours north of Sydney.

Peak fire danger season usually starts in mid-October in northern New South Wales and in December in southern parts of the state, according to the Bureau of Meteorology.

(Reporting by Stefica Bikes in Clarence Town; Writing by Alasdair Pal; Editing by Kate Mayberry)

Pakistani cricketers’ phones confiscated in England. Suspicion of match-fixing is the reason

The mobile phones were reportedly taken into PCB custody after Pakistan’s defeat in second Test against England, with data from the devices transferred before players returned home.

Debdutta Chakraborty

07 September, 2026 08:18 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

Pakistan's Imam-ul-Haq reacts after being dimissed by England pacer Jofra Archer | Lee Smith | Reuters

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

New Delhi: Pakistan’s England T our is getting murkier by the day. First, they considered not allowing players to return to the field at Lord’s after Sky News broadcast an interview with jailed former PM Imran Khan’s sons. Second, they fired seven players and the team’s head coach after the series loss. N ow they’ve confiscated the players’ phones on suspicions of match-fixing. It’s a never-ending loop of trouble and turmoil for the team.

Over the weekend, the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) launched an internal inquiry into player discipline following media reports concerning the activities of batters Imam-ul-Haq and Mohammad Rizwan during the team’s England tour. Their mobile phones were reportedly taken into PCB custody after Pakistan’s defeat in the second Test, with data from the devices transferred before the players returned home, reportedly as part of routine procedures.

PCB Director of Media and Digital Communications Amir Mir confirmed that the board was reviewing the matter, urging the public to rely on official statements rather than unverified reports circulating from external sources.

Show Full Article

“The Pakistan Cricket Board has initiated an internal disciplinary inquiry following media reports concerning discipline and conduct, which are currently being reviewed internally. The PCB handles such matters in accordance with its standard procedures. The process is being conducted under PCB regulations, ensuring that all concerned individuals are given due consideration,” Mir wrote on X.

According to Pakistani outlet 365 News , the phones will reportedly remain with the PCB until the third and final Test at Edgbaston, which begins on 9 September.

The investigation comes after major changes to Pakistan’s squad and coaching setup following their 194-run defeat to England at Lord’s, a result that gave England an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series.

The PCB released Mohammad Rizwan, Salman Ali Agha, Imam-ul-Haq, Ali Usman, Khurram Shahzad, Aamir Jamal and Muhammad Awais Zafar from the squad. Head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and bowling coach Umar Gul were also sent home, with Mike Hesson and Ashley Noffke brought in as their replacements.

Seven additional players were subsequently added to the squad for the Edgbaston Test. Saim Ayub and Abdullah Fazal have previous Test experience, while Arafat Minhas, Saad Baig, Muhammad Imran Randhawa, Razaullah and Mohammad Imran Junior are yet to make their Test debuts. Minhas, however, has already represented Pakistan in ODIs and T20Is.

Also read: Coke Studio’s Gen Z reboot Nu.WAV divides Pakistanis. ‘Give us back the old version’

‘Worst cricket board’ Pakistanis cannot take the downfall of cricket in their country anymore.

“Mobile phones of players in PCB custody This is quite unbelievable. What is our cricket board Upto ? Surely the worst cricket board in last 70 years of our existence,” former Sindh governor Mohammad Zubair wrote on X.

Given the joke it has become, a parody account on X added: “PCB has won more controversies than matches in this series”.

Former cricketer Tanveer called it a ‘shameful act’ symbolic of the fact that something of this scale has never occurred before.

Meanwhile, former cricketers Misbah-ul-Haq and Shoaib Akhtar have also spoken up. Akhtar said the Pakistan Cricket Board has lost faith in the current squad and is increasingly looking toward a younger generation of players.

Haq questioned the country’s broader cricketing structure and criticised what he sees as unequal treatment of local and foreign coaches, calling on the board to adopt a long-term strategy rather than repeatedly making decisions in response to short-term setbacks.

Speaking on the “OutSide EDGE” programme, Akhtar suggested that the PCB’s plans go beyond simply responding to Pakistan’s disappointing Test series in England. According to him, the board is preparing for a significant overhaul of the national team.

In the show, he also recalled a conversation with a PCB official who, according to Akhtar, indicated that the board’s expectations now rested primarily with the next generation of players being prepared for international cricket. Haq, however, called for patience, proper evaluation and a coherent long-term plan.

Pakistanis have no hope left. They have moved on from even blaming Mohsin Naqvi anymore.

“I am done blaming Mohsin Naqvi for PCB’s screw ups. The buck does NOT stop at Naqvi; it stops with the Patron-in-Chief of the PCB who is the PM of Pakistan @CMShehbaz. Sir, something is awfully broken and it is on you to now fix it. Hybrid or not, you need to exercise your powers. We need a dedicated PCB Chairman and not a bits-and-pieces part-timer. Yes, that may not fix everything, but start tackling the problem one thing at a time, please!”, Pakistani cricket commentator Shahab wrote on X .

(Edited by Saptak Datta)
